title: Quantum Cryptography: Applications and Future
description: QKD networks, repeaters, satellites, post-quantum crypto, and quantum money

questions.question: The main commercial application of quantum cryptography today is
options: quantum simulation of molecular spectra
quantum key distribution
quantum teleportation of data centres
quantum computing
questions.correctAnswer: quantum key distribution

questions.question: A QKD link supplies its users with
options: a random number generator with quantum-certified output
the encrypted message itself, secure without any classical cipher
a shared secret key, which is then used with a conventional symmetric cipher
a digital signature proving who signed the data
questions.correctAnswer: a shared secret key, which is then used with a conventional symmetric cipher

questions.question: The Chinese satellite Micius, launched in 2016, is notable for
options: storing quantum information in orbit for many years
operating the first quantum computer accessible over the internet
transmitting data faster than light between ground stations
demonstrating satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution over intercontinental distances
questions.correctAnswer: demonstrating satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution over intercontinental distances

questions.question: Satellite-based QKD is attractive because
options: the vacuum of space has very low loss, so one satellite can link ground stations thousands of kilometres apart
a satellite can amplify weak signals without adding noise
atmospheric turbulence cancels the loss that occurs in optical fibre
a satellite can copy unknown quantum states and forward them
questions.correctAnswer: the vacuum of space has very low loss, so one satellite can link ground stations thousands of kilometres apart

questions.question: The main limitation on fibre-based QKD over long distances is
options: the Doppler shift of the photons during transmission
the attenuation of light in the fibre, which reduces the photon arrival rate with distance
the limited bandwidth of the electro-optic modulator
polarisation drift caused by ambient magnetic fields
questions.correctAnswer: the attenuation of light in the fibre, which reduces the photon arrival rate with distance

questions.question: A quantum repeater is needed to extend a QKD link far beyond a short metropolitan distance because
options: ordinary optical amplifiers can restore the photon count without adding noise
the sifted key must be regenerated at every few kilometres
photons cannot be amplified without adding noise, so losses must be compensated by entanglement swapping
the fibre has to be cooled in order to reduce thermal noise
questions.correctAnswer: photons cannot be amplified without adding noise, so losses must be compensated by entanglement swapping

questions.question: In a quantum repeater network, entanglement swapping allows a
options: chain of repeaters that each share entanglement with their neighbours to extend entanglement end to end
single repeater to create a long-distance pair in one step, with no intermediate nodes
user to verify the key by exchanging whole photon states
middle station to measure the photons and learn the key directly
questions.correctAnswer: chain of repeaters that each share entanglement with their neighbours to extend entanglement end to end

questions.question: Building a full quantum-repeater network is difficult mainly because it requires
options: a much larger classical computer at every node
long-lived quantum memories and high-fidelity entanglement purification at many intermediate nodes
a synchronised atomic clock at each endpoint
optical amplifiers with unusually high gain
questions.correctAnswer: long-lived quantum memories and high-fidelity entanglement purification at many intermediate nodes

questions.question: Present-day QKD networks extend distance by using
options: trusted relay nodes that handle key material and must be physically secured
untrusted quantum repeaters that need no special protection
geostationary satellites above every major city
amplifiers that regenerate the photons without adding noise
questions.correctAnswer: trusted relay nodes that handle key material and must be physically secured

questions.question: A major practical limitation of current QKD systems is
options: the low efficiency of single-photon detectors, so most transmitted photons are never detected
the limited number of polarisation angles available within a basis
the inability of optical fibres to carry single photons at all
the short coherence time of the laser used to encode the bits
questions.correctAnswer: the low efficiency of single-photon detectors, so most transmitted photons are never detected

questions.question: Which effect degrades a long fibre-based QKD link?
options: polarisation drift caused by temperature fluctuations and by birefringence in the fibre
the magnetic field inside the fibre core
Doppler broadening of the laser linewidth
the gravitational redshift of the photons along the fibre
questions.correctAnswer: polarisation drift caused by temperature fluctuations and by birefringence in the fibre

questions.question: Why must commercial QKD devices be carefully characterised and tested?
options: classical key exchange always fails on optical links
an implementation can deviate from the ideal model and open side channels an eavesdropper can exploit
photons cannot be counted accurately in any detector
the laws of physics change at high key rates
questions.correctAnswer: an implementation can deviate from the ideal model and open side channels an eavesdropper can exploit

questions.question: Post-quantum cryptography refers to
options: classical algorithms such as lattice-, hash-, code- and multivariate-based schemes designed to resist quantum attacks
protocols that transmit key material over quantum channels
quantum algorithms that break current public-key systems faster
hardware that stores cryptographic keys on a quantum processor
questions.correctAnswer: classical algorithms such as lattice-, hash-, code- and multivariate-based schemes designed to resist quantum attacks

questions.question: Lattice-based post-quantum schemes such as LWE and Module-LWE are believed secure because
options: they require a quantum computer in order to be evaluated
their security follows directly from the no-cloning theorem
no efficient quantum algorithm is known for finding short vectors in high-dimensional lattices
they rest on the same hardness assumption as integer factoring
questions.correctAnswer: no efficient quantum algorithm is known for finding short vectors in high-dimensional lattices

questions.question: Hash-based post-quantum signature schemes are built on
options: the difficulty of solving a system of multivariate polynomial equations
the assumption that a cryptographic hash function has no practical preimage or collision
the difficulty of decoding a random linear code
the difficulty of computing a discrete logarithm
questions.correctAnswer: the assumption that a cryptographic hash function has no practical preimage or collision

questions.question: Code-based post-quantum schemes are based on
options: the presumed difficulty of finding a shortest vector in a lattice
the presumed difficulty of factoring large integers
the presumed difficulty of inverting a hash function
the presumed difficulty of decoding a random linear code
questions.correctAnswer: the presumed difficulty of decoding a random linear code

questions.question: Multivariate post-quantum schemes are based on
options: solving systems of multivariate polynomial equations over a finite field
factoring large composite integers
decoding a random linear code
finding collisions in a cryptographic hash function
questions.correctAnswer: solving systems of multivariate polynomial equations over a finite field

questions.question: The NIST post-quantum standardisation process is significant because
options: it has certified that RSA with a 2048-bit modulus can never be broken
it has produced standardised algorithms for the post-quantum era, encouraging migration before quantum computers arrive
it has replaced every public-key algorithm with a quantum one
it has banned all symmetric ciphers from government use
questions.correctAnswer: it has produced standardised algorithms for the post-quantum era, encouraging migration before quantum computers arrive

questions.question: A common migration strategy for organisations is
options: deploying hybrid classical and post-quantum key exchange, so security holds if either scheme is unbroken
moving all sensitive data into physically secured data centres
waiting until a cryptographically relevant quantum computer is announced
replacing all symmetric ciphers with one-time pads
questions.correctAnswer: deploying hybrid classical and post-quantum key exchange, so security holds if either scheme is unbroken

questions.question: QKD technology is being deployed in practice mainly in settings where long-term secrecy matters, such as
options: banks, government data centres and critical infrastructure networks
home routers, which already encrypt with one-time pads
public websites, which serve identical content to all visitors
consumer messaging apps, where keys are rotated every second
questions.correctAnswer: banks, government data centres and critical infrastructure networks

questions.question: Wiesner's quantum money scheme is secure because
options: the bank stores a token in a quantum state that a forger cannot copy
banknotes carry a quantum state that any bank can freely verify
the bank's private key is itself stored in a quantum register
a classical banknote can be made unforgeable with a very long secret number
questions.correctAnswer: the bank stores a token in a quantum state that a forger cannot copy

questions.question: A quantum digital signature provides
options: a shared secret key that both parties hold for encrypting future traffic
a certificate that a public key has never been exposed to an eavesdropper
proof that a message was sent by a particular sender and has not been altered
proof that a computation was performed by a quantum computer
questions.correctAnswer: proof that a message was sent by a particular sender and has not been altered

questions.question: What limits the immediate deployment of quantum cryptography networks?
options: the impossibility of generating random numbers quantum mechanically
the fact that quantum states cannot survive transmission through optical fibre
channel loss, decoherence and limited detector efficiency, together with the cost of specialised hardware
the absence of any agreed mathematical definition of entanglement
questions.correctAnswer: channel loss, decoherence and limited detector efficiency, together with the cost of specialised hardware
